sourcedFrom:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 (UNKNOWN - not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The 66 is Taurus's seven-shot .357 Magnum on the medium frame, and it lives inside the big REVOLVERS book - one manual carrying roughly 67 models at once. Hold on to one thing throughout: a procedure printed under another model's heading does not apply to your 66 because it is on the same page. What DOES apply, and is the difference between this gun and the small-frame Taurus guides, is the adjustable rear sight - the 66 sits in the ADJUSTABLE SIGHTS table, so the book's sight-adjustment section is genuinely yours, and there is a micrometric click sight on the topstrap you can knock out of zero with a careless cleaning rod.

steps.title: Find your 66 in the book's own table first
steps.action: The 66 sits in the MEDIUM FRAME ADJUSTABLE SIGHTS REVOLVERS table: .357 Magnum, DA/SA, seven rounds, 4-inch or 6-inch barrel. Note the word ADJUSTABLE in the heading - it decides which of this book's sight sections apply to you.
steps.prose: One book, sixty-odd revolvers, six specification tables. Reading the wrong row is not a small error here: the 83 and 86 sharing the 66's own table are .38 Special six-shooters, and the 96 is a .22. The caliber stamped on your barrel is the authority and the table is how you find the right row under it. Seven chambers, not six, is the 66's own signature.
steps.aside: One substitution is allowed and it is worth knowing: Taurus states .38 Special ammunition may be used in all their revolvers chambered for .357 Magnum, and that these are the only caliber substitutions that will function.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Medium Frame Adjustable Sights Revolvers - specifications, printed p.20 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: Seven chambers, single or double action
steps.action: Confirm the count as you open it: the 66 turns seven chambers around a central axis, and the shots may be fired single action by cocking the hammer or double action by pulling the trigger straight through.
steps.prose: Seven is the number to hold in your head for the rest of this clean, because the count is how you know you have finished. Going round once in one direction and stopping where you started is a discipline worth keeping on a seven-shot cylinder, where it is genuinely easy to lose your place.
steps.quote: The Taurus revolver has a swing out type cylinder with various numbers of chambers, turning around a central axis which allows you to fire (five, six, seven, eight or nine) shots.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Thumb piece FORWARD, cylinder out to the left
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger. Push the thumb piece forward with your right thumb and press the cylinder out to the left at the same time.
steps.prose: Forward is the whole trick, and it is where owners coming off other makes come unstuck: pressing the thumb piece down or inward simply pins the cylinder shut. The book's ATTENTION line lists exactly which models also need a front latch pressed - Models 30, 218, 416, 454, 444, 45, 513 and 513UL - and the 66 is not among them. On your gun one latch is all there is.
steps.quote: LOADING THE CYLINDER FOR .357 MAGNUM / .38 SPECIAL With the thumb of the right hand, push the thumb piece forward and at the same time press the cylinder, swinging it out to the left. ATTENTION: On Model 30, Model 218, Model 416, Model 454, Model 444, Model 45, Model 513 and Model 513UL using the left thumb, press down the front latch simultaneously.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Muzzle up, one sharp push on the extractor rod
steps.action: With the cylinder fully out, raise the muzzle and press sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure every case has left the cylinder.
steps.prose: Muzzle up, one decisive stroke. A .357 Magnum case is long and even a 4-inch 66's ejector rod does not give you the full case length of travel, so a half-hearted push can leave a case standing proud that drops back as the star returns. If one still sticks, a rod from the muzzle is the answer, not more force on the extractor.
steps.quote: Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure that all fired cartridges are ejected. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: Look AND feel every chamber - that is the working state
steps.action: Before any solvent comes out: muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, thumb piece depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and the revolver confirmed unloaded by looking into AND feeling each chamber.
steps.prose: Both senses. A brass case head sitting deep in a chamber reads as chamber wall to the eye at bench-light angles, and a fingertip finds what the light hides. From here the cylinder stays out - it is the only access this revolver gives you.
steps.quote: Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, (3) depress thumb piece and completely swing out the cylinder, (4) ensure the firearm is completely unloaded by looking and feeling each chamber.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Keep the cylinder empty unless you are actually firing
steps.action: Taurus's own warning is blunt: if dropped or struck, the revolver may fire. Keep the cylinder empty unless actually firing, and have the gun checked by a trained armourer or gunsmith if it is ever dropped.
steps.prose: This is the sentence that governs how a 66 lives on a cleaning bench. Loaded rounds do not come to the bench, and a revolver that hit the floor on the way there gets a function check before it gets solvent.
steps.quote:
WARNING - ANY GUN MAY FIRE IF DROPPED
If dropped or struck, the revolver may fire. Keep the cylinder empty unless actually firing!
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Ammunition, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Lead first, then carbon, then oil
steps.action: After shooting, remove all powder residue from the barrel and the adjacent areas with an appropriate brush. If you find lead particles in the barrel, scrub them with a brass brush drenched in oil, then lubricate.
steps.prose: Wet brass brush, never steel and never dry. Leading raises pressure, and it collects exactly where the gas is hottest - the forcing cone and the first inches of rifling. Cast-bullet practice loads put it there faster than jacketed ammunition.
steps.quote: 5. For cleaning after shooting, it is of special importance that all residues of powder be removed from barrel and other adjacent areas subject to such deposits, using an appropriate brush. If particles of lead are detected in barrel they must be scrubbed with a brass brush, drenched with oil.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Nothing here transfers to a look-alike
steps.action: Take this as belonging to this designation and the models named alongside it in the book's own exploded-view list, and nowhere else. Taurus prints the warning that look-alike firearms differ widely in the location and function of their controls.
steps.prose: The tell is always a control that behaves the other way. Taurus's thumb piece slides toward the muzzle; most other makers' cylinder latches push rearward or inward. If pushing it forward does nothing, stop - you are not holding this gun.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Ammunition, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: The adjustable sight IS yours - so protect it while you clean
steps.action: Your 66 has a micrometric click rear sight adjustable for windage and elevation. The book's External Adjustable Sight procedure applies to it: elevation screw counterclockwise raises the rear sight and raises the point of impact, clockwise lowers both.
steps.prose: This is the section a small-frame fixed-sight Taurus guide has to exclude, and it is the reason this guide is not that guide. The practical consequence at the bench is simple: do not rest a cleaning rod or a bore guide against the rear sight blade and do not use it as a handle. A micrometric sight holds zero by detent, and it will move if you lean on it.
steps.quote: External Adjustable Sight Models Only To adjust, make sure the firearm is unloaded and always keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction. If possible, leave the cylinder open during adjustment. To raise the rear sight, turn the elevation adjusting screw counterclockwise. To lower the rear sight, turn the screw clockwise.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Adjusting the Sights, printed p.36 (PDF p.19)

steps.title: Windage on the same sight, and note your setting before you start
steps.action: The rear sight also adjusts for windage - the windage screw clockwise moves the notch right, counter-clockwise moves it left. Count and write down where yours sits before a heavy clean, so you can put it back if it gets nudged.
steps.prose: Nobody records their zero until the first time they lose it. A click count on a slip of paper in the case costs nothing and saves a range session. Adjust only with the revolver unloaded and, as the book asks, with the cylinder left open if you can.
steps.quote: The rear sight can also be adjusted for windage. Turn the windage adjusting screw clockwise to move the notch to right side, and counter-clockwise to move the notch to left side.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Adjusting the Sights, printed p.36 (PDF p.19)

steps.title: Field strip complete - the barrel stays on
steps.action: Cylinder swung out and every chamber empty. That is the whole field strip. Taurus states the revolver is cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions with no disassembly needed, and then says plainly: do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.prose: Where disassembly genuinely is necessary the book's route is the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer - not the bench. The exploded view at the back is headed 'Model: 66, 83, 86, 96'; it is a parts list for ordering, with no sequence attached, and it is not an invitation to take anything off.
steps.quote: 1. The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

deepAbsentReason: The Taurus REVOLVERS book publishes no disassembly for any of the roughly 67 models it covers. Its care section opens by saying the firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly, and adds flatly 'Do not disassemble the barrel.' Where disassembly is genuinely necessary it routes the revolver to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer. The nine exploded views at the back are parts diagrams headed with model lists and carry no order of operations. ⛔ PROHIBITED IS PER-PROCEDURE, NOT PER-FAMILY: what Taurus forbids is disassembling the barrel, not cleaning the gun - the forbidden operation is carried in this spec's `prohibits` field and the routine clean is published in full. Nothing deeper is walked because nothing deeper is published.

cleaning.name: BORE, FORCING CONE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Remove all residues of powder from the barrel and the adjacent areas with an appropriate brush
If particles of lead are detected in the barrel, scrub them with a brass brush drenched with oil, then lubricate as described
Work the forcing cone hard - it takes the gas cutting and most of the leading
Brush every chamber and follow with a dry patch, then check the bore against a light
Clean before shooting more than 200 rounds in a row

cleaning.name: CYLINDER FACE, STAR & CRANE
tasks: Take the carbon ring off the front face of the cylinder - it is what eventually stops the cylinder closing
Push the extractor rod back and clean behind the star; grit under the star holds it proud and the cylinder will not close on it
Wipe the crane and the frame window and confirm the cylinder sits flush when closed
Use no abrasive material anywhere on the cylinder - the book bans it outright on the titanium guns and it is bad practice on all of them

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR, OIL & STORAGE
tasks: Rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth and proceed the same way through the bore; remove the excess but leave a thin protecting film
Remove dust from all crevices with a small, clean brush
Keep the revolver away from materials that attract moisture or carry acidity, and avoid cloth holsters that hold damp
For long storage take extra care with the metal surfaces against corrosion
A revolver fitted with a laser must not be cleaned in a well or ultrasonic machine that submerges it

reassembly: Nothing was removed, so nothing is refitted. Let the extractor rod return fully before the cylinder goes home.
Close the cylinder gently until it latches - never flick it shut, which knocks the crane out of true and starts the cylinder binding.
Rotate the closed cylinder by hand through a full turn and feel the cylinder stop drop into each notch.
fncheck: With all seven chambers confirmed empty: the cylinder should latch under light thumb pressure with no perceptible side play; hand rotation should feel the cylinder stop engage at each notch; the hammer should hold at full cock without following; the transfer bar must stay clear of the firing pin until the trigger is pulled fully through and drop back as it returns; and both single and double action should reset positively when the trigger returns all the way forward. Check the rear sight blade has not been nudged - a micrometric click sight is held by detent, not by friction. Taurus's standing advice for their revolvers is to keep the cylinder empty unless actually firing.
